title: The Workbench on a Real Repo

questions.question: What is the goal of running the same task through prompt-only and workbench-guided pipelines?
options: To compare models
To produce a before/after report you can hand to a skeptic with numbers, not arguments
To pick a vendor
To benchmark GPUs
questions.explanation: The numbers do the arguing; the case is made on a real-feeling task, not a toy.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the five outcomes measured?
options: tests_actually_run
acceptance_met
files_outside_scope
model_perplexity
questions.explanation: The five are tests_actually_run, acceptance_met, files_outside_scope, handoff_quality, reviewer_total.

questions.question: What role do README.md and scripts/release.sh play in the sample app, per the lesson?
options: They hold the acceptance criteria the verification gate checks
They are the two files the task explicitly asks the agent to edit
They are forbidden-zone bait, testing if a run stays in scope
They store the before/after report the lesson later generates
questions.explanation: The lesson describes README.md and scripts/release.sh in the sample app as forbidden-zone bait.

questions.question: What does the prompt-only pipeline skip that the workbench-guided pipeline includes, per the lesson?
options: Reading the README before editing any files in the repo
Running the test suite at any point during the session
Editing app.py to add the validation the task requested
A scope contract, a verification gate, and a reviewer
questions.explanation: The lesson lists the prompt-only pipeline as read README, read app.py, edit files, claim done; the workbench-guided pipeline adds the scope contract, feedback runner, verification gate, reviewer, and handoff steps.

questions.question: What is the task both pipelines run in the lesson?
options: Add rate limiting to /signup and log every rejected attempt
Migrate /signup from synchronous to asynchronous request handling
Add a password-strength meter to the signup form's frontend
Validate /signup: reject short passwords, return a typed 422
questions.explanation: The lesson states the task as: add input validation to /signup, reject passwords shorter than 8 characters, return 422 with a typed error envelope, and add a test that proves the new behavior.

questions.question: Why does the lesson measure tests_actually_run as one of the five outcomes?
options: Because CI billing is charged per test that actually runs
Because the reviewer agent only reads tests run more than once
Because handoff quality is scored solely on total test count
Because most 'tests passed' claims are otherwise unverifiable
questions.explanation: The lesson's outcomes table gives the reason for tests_actually_run as: most 'tests passed' claims are unverifiable.

questions.question: Why does files_outside_scope matter as one of the five measured outcomes, per the lesson?
options: Because it is the only outcome the verification gate can compute
Because it directly sets the reviewer_total score by formula
Because it is the cheapest of the five outcomes to measure
Because scope creep is the dominant silent failure mode here
questions.explanation: The lesson's outcomes table gives the reason for files_outside_scope as: scope creep is the dominant silent failure.
